about: covenant's side of the receipt interop test vectors promised in Hugging Face thread 180706 post #22. Canonicalization: RFC 8785 (JCS) plus profile rules P1-P6 below. TEST KEYS ONLY: derived as sha256 of the phrases given, so every signature is reproducible; not covenant's receipt signer. covenant's production receipts do NOT yet canonicalize with JCS: each vector carries the current production canonical form where it differs.

profile_rules.P1: reject duplicate member names at parse
profile_rules.P2: reject any string (name or value) that holds a lone surrogate or is not already Unicode NFC. Cost: some valid JCS input is refused -- RFC 8785's own 3.2.3 sorting sample contains U+FB33, which NFC maps to U+05D3 U+05BC
profile_rules.P3: reject any number TOKEN whose magnitude exceeds 2^53-1, in any spelling (plain or exponent form), checked on the token with exact decimal arithmetic before any conversion to a double; carry such values as strings
profile_rules.P4: exclude the proof at the top level only; nested 'proof' members are signed content
profile_rules.P6a: relying party rejects a domain other than the one it expects
profile_rules.P6b: relying party rejects an audience other than itself
profile_rules.P6c: relying party rejects a chain_id other than the one it requires
profile_rules.P7: a verifier takes each signer's framing from the discovery document and never tries the other one
profile_rules.P6d: relying party rejects a receipt with no nonce, or a (signer, nonce) it has already accepted, and records the pair on acceptance. The check-and-record must be atomic and durable (concurrent presentations, restarts); these vectors cannot test that, a verifier's own tests must

issuer: the replay key is (signer, nonce) and nothing in the signed bytes names an issuer: the signing key IS the issuer. A design choice; an issuer field in the signed content is the alternative
not_covered: number tokens that lose precision through a double (1.00000000000000001 canonicalizes to 1): P3 bounds magnitude only. Amounts in this profile are strings, which is why
the trust root: N02 checks a signature against the signer a discovery document names; nothing here establishes that the discovery document itself is genuine (DNS/TLS, or an out-of-band pin)
independence: results_by_our_verifier come from this file's own verifier, which shares its canonicalizer with the generator. A second implementation's results are the real cross-check
new_fields: domain, audience, chain_id and nonce are fields of this proposed profile; the receipt exchanged in the thread on 2026-10-21 had none of them
signing: deterministic ECDSA (RFC 6979, as eth_account does it): regenerating this file reproduces every signature byte for byte
framing_choice: EIP-191, with each signer's framing pinned in the discovery document (P7). EIP-712, raised in the thread as the clean route for domain separation, is not used here and is still open
reject_vectors: each profile-reject vector is signed (by A and by C) over the bytes a verifier WITHOUT the rule computes, so such a verifier would accept it and only the rule can reject it; the lone surrogate and 1e400 are the exceptions: no canonical bytes can exist for them

framings.hex-text: EIP-191 personal_sign over the 64-char lowercase hex of SHA-256(canonical) (covenant)
framings.digest-bytes: EIP-191 personal_sign over the raw 32-byte SHA-256 (Agent Embassy)

A.phrase: covenant receipt interop TEST KEY A -- never sign anything real

C.phrase: covenant receipt interop TEST KEY C -- never sign anything real

B.phrase: covenant receipt interop TEST KEY B -- never sign anything real

discovery_document.rule: P7: a verifier takes the framing from this document, by signer, and never tries the other one

rfc8785_selfcheck: Appendix B (26 numbers incl. NaN/Infinity rejected), 3.2.3 sort order, 3.2.4 bytes: all pass

negatives.why: P7 -- the same, in the other direction

replay_sequence.note: run against a FRESH relying party configured as above; the only vectors that share verifier state. Each step presents one receipt with one signer's signature; every receipt carries its own unused nonce except where a step reuses one on purpose, so each rejection can only come from the rule named in expect_reason

steps.why: the same nonce from a different signer: the replay key is the (signer, nonce) pair
absent-field bypass: without the presence check this is accepted the first time
